Definition: Extent to which the national digital identity system is integrated with the data exchange for identity verification and authentication
Comments: Morocco launched a national digital identity platform in May 2022. Citizens can scan their NFC-enabled CNIE (national electronic identity card) to create a digital ID using the My Digital Identity app. The platform is based on DGSN's Trusted Third Party platform, sharing exact personal data from identity cards with service providers. Supports fingerprint, face recognition, or OTP multi-factor authentication. Digital ID is integrated with multiple public and private online services. Score 4: partially integrated.

Definition: Whether primary laws, acts, or legal instruments exist that establish authority for cross-government data sharing and govern the data exchange system
Comments: Morocco has multiple enabling laws: Personal Data Protection (Law No. 09-08, 2009) - establishes CNDP and governs data processing. Electronic Data Exchange (Law No. 53-05) - explicitly supports secure legal data exchanges. Simplification of Administrative Procedures (Law No. 55.19) and Public Services Charter (Law No. 54.19) mandate digital service delivery. Inter-administration Data Interoperability framework exists (referenced in Digital Morocco 2030). ADD was created by Law No. 61.16 (2017). Digital X.0 bill under review (2025) will further strengthen the framework. Score 3: yes, enabling legislation exists.

Definition: Whether a formal strategy or policy document exists specifically for government data exchange and interoperability
Comments: Morocco has a comprehensive and long-standing digital strategy framework: Maroc Numeric 2013, Maroc Numeric 2020, and Digital Morocco 2030 (launched Sep 2024). The 2030 strategy explicitly addresses e-government digitization, interoperability, unified portal, AI, and data governance. Digital X.0 bill (2025) focuses on three strategic pillars: data governance, digital identity, and interoperability. ADD was created by Law 61.16 (2017) as the implementing body. Ministry of Digital Transition and Administrative Reform leads strategy. Morocco chairs CAITA (Smart Africa) and is developing Africa's first cross-border data exchange guidelines. Score 4: comprehensive strategy exists.

Definition: Is artificial intelligence integrated into the data exchange for data quality, fraud detection or predictive analytics
Comments: Morocco is developing AI capabilities for government. The Digital Morocco 2030 strategy identifies AI as a key catalyst with plans to use AI to enhance data management and improve service quality. Morocco's Digital X.0 law (under review 2025) focuses on AI governance and data governance as core pillars. The interoperability platform (launched 2022 by ADD/Minsait) uses IoT and Big Data capabilities. Morocco hosted Africa's first National AI Summit in July 2025 alongside CAITA cross-border data exchange guidelines development. The Maroc Digital 2030 strategy mentions AI in public services. However, AI specifically integrated into data exchange for quality/fraud across 2+ systems is still in early/piloting stage. Score 3: piloting.

Definition: Current operational status of the data exchange system
Comments: Morocco's Agency for Digital Development (ADD) launched a national e-government interoperability platform in September 2022 (developed by Minsait). The platform is operational with the Single Social Register (RSU), MASSAR school management system, and social programs connected. Morocco has 300+ digital public services for citizens and 200+ for businesses. The platform is an open IoT/Big Data system enabling secure data exchange across public administrations with different IT systems. National digital identity platform launched May 2022 (My Digital Identity app linked to CNIE via DGSN). Status: partially operational - multiple systems connected but not all government systems integrated. Score 4: partially operational.

Definition: Provisions ensuring national control over government data and protecting against unauthorized foreign access
Comments: Digital Morocco 2030 adopts a hybrid cloud model with 'sovereign cloud' for sensitive/public sector data and public cloud for businesses. Sovereign cloud will be 'managed by Moroccan operators' for sensitive data. Digital X.0 bill (2025) includes data sovereignty as a key pillar with a 'traceable consent mechanism to regulate data exchanges'. Law 09-08 restricts cross-border data transfers. CNDP enforces data protection. However, Morocco's data localization requirements are not as strong as some African peers and the sovereign cloud model is still being implemented. Score 3: strong provisions yet unenforced (hybrid sovereign cloud in development).
